report.summary: Read chunk 1 of daedalus/mapping/inventory.py; verified docstring/comment claims against the code present.

handoff.purpose: Module docstring, constants, helpers for digest and small derivations.

symbols.name: INVENTORY_REL
symbols.note: Relative path to the inventory file.

symbols.name: DIGEST_KEY
symbols.note: Key name for digest in document.

symbols.name: ENV_HUMAN_FIELDS
symbols.note: Tuple of human-owned env var fields.

symbols.name: _HUMAN_TOP_KEYS
symbols.note: Frozenset of top-level keys excluded from digest.

symbols.name: STATUS_BY_CLASS
symbols.note: Mapping of reach classification to inventory status.

symbols.name: _TOKEN_RE
symbols.note: Regex for tokens that could name a module.

symbols.name: _strip_human
symbols.note: Builds mechanical projection of a document, removing human fields and blocks.

symbols.name: _digest
symbols.note: Computes sha256 digest over stripped projection.

symbols.name: digest_ok
symbols.note: Checks whether document's own digest matches recomputed digest.

symbols.name: _dotted
symbols.note: Converts relative path to dotted module name.

symbols.name: _method_of
symbols.note: Returns HTTP method from handler name suffix, or ''.

symbols.name: _pyproject_packages
symbols.note: Reads explicit packages list from pyproject.toml; returns [] on absence/unreadable.

claims.text: The module census and its status -- wired / island / shim / unknown -- straight off daedalus.mapping.reach.analyse's classification
claims.why: STATUS_BY_CLASS maps reach classes to statuses, but the actual use of analyse's classification is in later chunks; this chunk only defines the mapping.

claims.text: entrypoints, entry_kinds, importers and tests per module
claims.why: No code in this chunk derives these fields; they appear only in the docstring.

claims.text: the CLI dispatch table and the HTTP route table, from the entry points
claims.why: No CLI or route table derivation code appears in this chunk.

claims.text: every environment switch, where it is read, whether it is dark and whether any document mentions it, from daedalus.mapping.switches
claims.why: No switch-related code in this chunk.

claims.text: two kinds of stale: a package this repo's own packaging metadata promises that is not on disk, and a __pycache__ whose sources are gone
claims.why: The stale sweep is implemented in later chunks; this chunk only defines _STALE_SKIP_DIRS and STATUS_STALE.

claims.text: the packaging gap in the other direction -- a package on disk that a wheel would not contain
claims.why: No code in this chunk performs that check.

claims.text: editing a note, a name or a kind is legal and does not trip the gate
claims.why: FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS includes name, kind, notes; _strip_human removes them from features (line ~140-143).

claims.text: editing a status, a test list or an island entry DOES trip it
claims.why: The digest covers all derived fields; status and test lists are not in human field sets, so edits change the digest.

claims.text: Annotations carry human fields ONLY. An annotation cannot set status and cannot add a module
claims.why: This chunk does not contain annotation handling logic; only _HUMAN_TOP_KEYS lists 'annotations' as human.

claims.text: The mechanical projection of a whole document. Everything a human is allowed to write is removed
claims.why: The function skips _HUMAN_TOP_KEYS and filters human fields per record type.

claims.text: A hash over the derived half only. Canonical JSON, sorted keys
Public for the same reason daedalus.mapping.drift.digest_ok is: any consumer that RANKS WORK out of these lists rather than rescanning has to ask this first
claims.why: Reference to another module's function; not verifiable in this chunk.

claims.text: A handler that does not follow the convention yields "" rather than a fabricated method
Starts at a letter or underscore so "/api/x" and ".claude/y" do not produce a phantom leading-punctuation token
claims.why: Regex starts with [A-Za-z_], so leading punctuation is not matched.

claims.text: An unreadable or absent pyproject yields an empty list
claims.why: The function body is cut off; the try block is not fully visible. The claim mentions absence/unreadable, but we cannot see the except clause.

claims.text: The revision, and only the revision. branch and dirty move without the architecture moving
a gate that goes red because somebody has unsaved edits is a gate people switch off
claims.why: The code excludes 'dirty' from the digest projection.

observations.what: The _pyproject_packages function body is truncated; the try/except logic is not visible, so the claim about unreadable pyproject yielding [] is not fully verifiable.
The comment for _TOKEN_RE says the regex avoids phantom tokens from leading punctuation, and the regex indeed starts with [A-Za-z_], so the claim is consistent.
The docstring claims that the module derives module census, entrypoints, etc., but this chunk only provides constants and small helpers; the actual derivation is in later chunks.
